buckets.title: Pinnacle NLM momentum-transfer-rate extension
buckets.badge_reason: The arithmetic is modest, but the learner must convert per-item momentum into a per-time transfer and keep recoil forces assigned to the correct body.

conventions.statement: Choose the item/body and inertial frame before calculating momentum change.
Momentum becomes an average force only after a time interval or item rate is introduced.
Use Newton III to place the equal-and-opposite recoil interaction on the launcher, not on the bullet's own FBD.

scope.covers: p=mv for one emitted item, Delta p over a stated interval, F_avg=Delta p/Delta t, and steady identical-item momentum flow such as bullets per second with equal-and-opposite average recoil interpretation.
excluded: Full collision or explosion momentum-conservation curriculum.
Rocket equation or continuously varying-mass dynamics.
Instantaneous force reconstruction from a general time-dependent momentum function.
Default placement in ordinary Grade-9 NLM progression.

capabilities.action: Relate a stated momentum change to average force, including steady repeated-item momentum transfer and equal-and-opposite recoil.
capabilities.success_criterion: Computes p=mv for the chosen item, forms Delta p in one frame, converts total momentum change over a stated interval or repeated-item rate into F_avg=Delta p/Delta t, checks force units, and assigns the recoil partner to the launcher/body rather than cancelling forces on one FBD.

microtopics.title: Convert repeated-item momentum transfer into average recoil force
microtopics.badge_reason: The key failure is dimensional/model selection: one bullet's momentum is not a force until the learner introduces the transfer interval or firing rate.
entry_assumptions: Can distinguish the bullet/item from the launcher and place Newton-third-law partners on different bodies.
Can multiply mass by velocity and preserve a one-dimensional sign convention.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Repeated per-item momentum changes accumulate over time, so a firing/ejection rate converts momentum per item into momentum per second and therefore average force.

teaching_path.action: Choose the emitted item and signed direction; write p_i=m v_i and p_f=m v_f for that item.
teaching_path.why_valid: The rate calculation must start from a well-defined momentum change of one chosen item.
teaching_path.output: Example from rest to +v: Delta p_item = m v.

teaching_path.action: If r identical items are emitted each second, sum their momentum changes over one second.
teaching_path.why_valid: Repeated identical changes add linearly in the counting interval.
teaching_path.output: In 1 s, Delta p_total = r Delta p_item.

teaching_path.action: Divide the total momentum transfer by the interval to obtain average force.
teaching_path.why_valid: Momentum divided by time has force dimensions and is the interval-average rate of momentum change.
teaching_path.output: For the 1 s count: |F_avg| = r |Delta p_item| = r m |v_f-v_i|.

teaching_path.action: Use Newton III to assign the equal-and-opposite average recoil to the launcher, then check units.
teaching_path.why_valid: The bullet force and launcher recoil are interaction partners on different bodies; kg m/s^2 is N.
teaching_path.output: Emitted momentum is forward; launcher recoil is opposite; r m Delta v has units N.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The recoil force is numerically equal to one bullet's momentum.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A bullet momentum has units kg m/s. What factor is needed before it can equal a force?
misconceptions.repair: Introduce time: divide total momentum transfer by seconds, or multiply per-bullet momentum by bullets per second.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Bullet and launcher forces cancel on the bullet FBD.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Does the launcher recoil force act on the bullet?
misconceptions.repair: No. Third-law partners act on different bodies; calculate the bullet momentum transfer, then place the equal-and-opposite recoil on the launcher.

exit_task.prompt: A launcher fires identical bullets from rest. Each bullet leaves with forward momentum p and the steady firing rate is r bullets per second. State the average recoil-force magnitude and direction.

answer.summary: The average recoil-force magnitude is r p, directed opposite the outgoing bullets.
reasoning: Each bullet gains forward momentum p.
In one second, r bullets gain total forward momentum r p.
Average force magnitude is momentum transferred per second: r p.
Newton III places an equal-and-opposite average interaction on the launcher.
answer.check: r has unit 1/s, so r p has kg m/s^2 = N; reversing the firing direction reverses recoil.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The symbolic result directly tests the steady repeated-item momentum-rate model.

microtopics.research_contribution: Directly answers the distinct learner action identified by the owner-supplied machine-gun item, after the first friction/connected NLM production slice has been separated.

predict.prompt: If momentum per bullet is unchanged but the firing rate doubles, what happens to average recoil-force magnitude?

attempt.produces: Per-item momentum change, conversion to per-second momentum transfer, and recoil-body interpretation.

rubric.criterion: Introduces a time/rate before calling the result a force.
Places recoil on the launcher rather than cancelling it on the bullet.

accepted: F_avg=(momentum change per bullet)*(bullets per second), with opposite recoil on launcher.
rejected: Set force equal to one bullet momentum without a time/rate factor.

route.ask: What quantity does one bullet gain?
How much of that quantity is transferred in one second at rate r?
route.why_this_ask: Builds the rate without handing over the final formula.

route.ask: Which body receives the opposite interaction?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Teaching states the momentum-rate sequence; reconstruction starts from one item and one second, then lets the learner infer the force relation.

boundary_test.prompt: Does this capability by itself determine two unknown final velocities after a collision?
boundary_test.answer: No. That requires an additional system momentum-conservation model, which is outside this extension.
boundary_test.confirms: The extension is momentum-transfer rate, not a collision curriculum.

relations.expression: p = m v; F_avg = Delta p / Delta t; steady identical items at rate r: |F_avg| = r |Delta p_item|
relations.meaning: Average external force equals momentum transferred per unit time; for identical emitted items at a steady rate, their per-item momentum changes add linearly over the counting interval.

symbols.meaning: Linear momentum of the chosen item/body
Constant item/body mass for the stated change
Velocity in the chosen inertial frame
Momentum change over the stated interval
Average net force associated with the momentum change
Steady number of identical items transferred per second
Momentum change of one emitted item

conditions: Momentum and velocity refer to the same chosen item/body and one inertial frame.
The first-slice relation treats the item mass as constant over its stated momentum change.
F_avg is the average net force associated with the stated momentum transfer over Delta t.
For a steady stream of identical items, the per-item momentum change and item rate refer to the same counting interval.
The equal-and-opposite recoil interpretation belongs to the launcher/body on the other side of the interaction, not to the emitted item's own free-body equation.

derivation.action: Choose one emitted item and one inertial frame, then calculate its initial and final momentum p_i=m v_i and p_f=m v_f.
derivation.why_valid: Momentum change is meaningful only for a specified body/item in one frame.

derivation.action: For one interval, sum the item momentum changes and divide by Delta t.
derivation.why_valid: Average force is momentum transferred per unit time over the interval.

derivation.action: For a steady rate r identical items per second, replace the count over one second by r.
derivation.why_valid: Each item contributes the same Delta p_item, so total momentum transferred in one second is r Delta p_item.
derivation.output: |F_avg| = r |Delta p_item| for the emitted stream; recoil has equal magnitude and opposite direction on the launcher.

derivation.why_valid: (1/s)(kg m/s)=kg m/s^2=N, and Newton III puts the reaction on the other body.
derivation.output: Momentum-rate result has force units; recoil arrow is on the launcher FBD.

limits: This relation is used here for interval-average/steady-rate reasoning, not general instantaneous force histories.
No collision-conservation law is implied by this single-body momentum-transfer calculation.
Variable-mass rocket dynamics require additional system-boundary analysis and are excluded.
checks: Doubling r with per-item Delta p fixed doubles |F_avg|.
If Delta p_item is zero, the corresponding average momentum-transfer force is zero.
Recoil direction is opposite the emitted stream's momentum gain.
